Meditations on Proverbs 3 - Part 5Proverbs 3:9-10Honor the LORD with your wealthand with the firstfruits of all your produce;then your barns will be filled with plenty,and your vats will be bursting with wine.Summary: If you want to have everything you need and more, honor God with what you have and the first of all your income.Honor the LORD with your wealth, means to use what you currently have to honor God. In Luke Jesus tells a story of a wealthy man that did not honor God with his wealth.Luke 12:16-21And he told them a parable, saying, "The land of a rich man produced plentifully, and he thought to himself, âWhat shall I do, for I have nowhere to store my crops?' And he said, âI will do this: I will tear down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods. And I will say to my soul, "Soul, you have ample goods laid up for many years; relax, eat, drink, be merry."' But God said to him, âFool! This night your soul is required of you, and the things you have prepared, whose will they be?' So is the one who lays up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God."Contrast with Corenius, a wealthy man who did honor God.Acts 10:1-5At Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion of what was known as the Italian Cohort, a devout man who feared God with all his household, gave alms generously to the people, and prayed continually to God. About the ninth hour of the day he saw clearly in a vision an angel of God come in and say to him, "Cornelius." And he stared at him in terror and said, "What is it, Lord?" And he said to him, "Your prayers and your alms have ascended as a memorial before God. And now send men to Joppa and bring one Simon who is called Peter.It doesn't matter how much or how little you have, you can honor God with it. You must prove that you can honor God with little before He can entrust you with more.Luke 16:10-13"One who is faithful in a very little is also faithful in much, and one who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much. If then you have not been faithful in the unrighteous wealth, who will entrust to you the true riches? And if you have not been faithful in that which is another's, who will give you that which is your own? No servant can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and money."The second part of Proverbs 3:9 is to honor God "with the firstfruits of all your produce". This was written to an agricultural society, so for us this means to honor God with the firstfruits (the first and best) of all our income. This includes the tithe.Malachi 3:8-10Will man rob God? Yet you are robbing me. But you say, âHow have we robbed you?' In your tithes and contributions. You are cursed with a curse, for you are robbing me, the whole nation of you. Bring the full tithe into the storehouse, that there may be food in my house. And thereby put me to the test, says the LORD of hosts, if I will not open the windows of heaven for you and pour down for you a blessing until there is no more need.Taking 10% of all your income and bringing it to God first - before paying rent, utilities, etc - is a way of honoring God and trusting that He will be true to His word.The promise is that "your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will be bursting with wine." Written to an agricultural society, this would mean blessing on crops and livestock, and we see exactly this blessing in Deuteronomy 28. Note however, that this is dependent on obeying God's commands. In this same way, the promise in Proverbs 3:10 is also dependent on following Proverbs 3:1-9. Deuteronomy 28:1-12"And if you faithfully obey the voice of the LORD your God, being careful to do all his commandments that I command you today, â¦ all these blessings shall come upon you and overtake youâ¦ Blessed shall you be in the city, and blessed shall you be in the field. Blessed shall be the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground and the fruit of your cattle, the increase of your herds and the young of your flock. Blessed shall be your basket and your kneading bowl. Blessed shall you be when you come in, and blessed shall you be when you go out. â¦ The LORD will command the blessing on you in your barns and in all that you undertake. And he will bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you. â¦ And the LORD will make you abound in prosperity, in the fruit of your womb and in the fruit of your livestock and in the fruit of your ground, within the land that the LORD swore to your fathers to give you. The LORD will open to you his good treasury, the heavens, to give the rain to your land in its season and to bless all the work of your hands. And you shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow.Many of us are not farmers today, but these verses still apply. They speak of blessing in our occupation, blessing in our income, protection of what we own. Not living paycheck to paycheck, but having enough to live on and enjoy life and still put money in the bank. And why will God bless us this way? Because He knows that we will continue to "Honor the LORD with your wealth, the firstfruits of all your crops [income]". God blesses us because He loves us and wants to bless us yes, but also so that we can bless others and extend his kingdom. If we are not rich toward God with these blessings, we become like the man in Luke 12.

Meditations on Proverbs 3 - Part 4Proverbs 3:7-8Be not wise in your own eyes;fear the LORD, and turn away from evil.It will be healing to your fleshand refreshment to your bones.Summary: If you want physical healing and refreshment, don't be a "know it all", but fear God and avoid evil.This passage starts with a contrast. Being wise in your own eyes vs. fearing the LORD. To better understand these concepts, let's look at a few more verses.Proverbs 12:15The way of a fool is *right in his own eyes*,but a wise man listens to advice.Proverbs 26:12Do you see a man who is *wise in his own eyes*?There is more hope for a fool than for him.Proverbs 26:16The sluggard is *wiser in his own eyes*than seven men who can answer sensibly.From these three verses, we can understand that being wise in your own eyes is synonymous with refusing the advice, instruction, and rebuke of others. In this state of mind, you are beyond hope because you will not listen to anyone but yourself. One who is wise in their own eyes would reject even the words of God.In contrastProverbs 9:9-10Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be still wiser;teach a righteous man, and he will increase in learning.The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom,and the knowledge of the Holy One is insight.AndProverbs 15:31-33The ear that listens to life-giving reproofwill dwell among the wise.Whoever ignores instruction despises himself,but he who listens to reproof gains intelligence.The fear of the LORD is instruction in wisdom,and humility comes before honor.So we see that being wise means being teachable and the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom. Job 28 is a magnificent piece of poetry on finding wisdom. It ends with the conclusion that God is the only one who knows where wisdom can be found, so men can only be wise by fearing God.Job 28:20-28"From where, then, does wisdom come?And where is the place of understanding?It is hidden from the eyes of all livingand concealed from the birds of the airâ¦"God understands the way to it,and he knows its place.For he looks to the ends of the earthand sees everything under the heavensâ¦he saw it [wisdom] and declared it [wisdom];he established it [wisdom], and searched it [wisdom] out.And he said to man,âBehold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom,and to turn away from evil is understanding.'"As we choose to fear the LORD (which includes listening to His instruction) and turn away from evil, why does this bring healing and refreshment? I think that scripture points out a couple of reasons.First, fearing God means being attentive to HIs words and His words themselves are life.Proverbs 4:20-22My son, be attentive to my words;incline your ear to my sayings.Let them not escape from your sight;keep them within your heart.For they are life to those who find them,and healing to all their flesh.Second, fearing God means obeying His commands and obedience to His commands brings blessing and health.Deuteronomy 7:12,15"And because you listen to these rules and keep and do them, the LORD your God will keep with you the covenant and the steadfast love that he swore to your fathers. He will love you, bless you, and multiply you. â¦ And the LORD will take away from you all sickness, and none of the evil diseases of Egypt, which you knew, will he inflict on you, but he will lay them on all who hate you.

Meditations on Proverbs 3 - Part 3Proverbs 3:5-6Trust in the LORD with all your heart,and do not lean on your own understanding.In all your ways acknowledge him,and he will make straight your paths.Summary: If you want to know which way to take and have the obstacles removed, acknowledge God and not your own understanding.Trust - Hebrew bÌ±aÌtÌ£ahÌ£. Literally to hide in for refuge. Figuratively trust and confidence in, to be bold and confident, to be sure.Heart - figuratively the center of anything. The core of your being: mental, physical, and emotional. This is the 3rd time that the word "heart" has been used in five verses.- Let your *heart* keep my commandmentsâ¦and peace they will add to you- Write them [love and faithfulness] on the tablet of your *heart*â¦so you will find favorâ¦in the sight of God- Trust in the LORD with all your *heart*â¦and He will make straight your pathsOnce our hearts are keeping God's commands and have love and faithfulness written on them, we are ready to trust in the LORD with all of our hearts. Notice that we are not told to trust with our mind or understanding. It's actually our understanding that we are trying to bypass (and lean not on your own understanding v5). This is a picture of walking by faith (trust in God) and not by sight (natural senses and understanding).Verse 6 starts with, "In all your ways acknowledge him." The word translated "acknowledge" literally means "to know (intimately)", but is used figuratively in many different senses. So we could say, "In all your ways seek Him, know Him, acknowledge Him, follow Him." In everything you do in life, look for God and seek to obey and worship Him.This passage ends with, "and He will make straight your paths". The word translated straight can also have the sense of making your paths (way of living) smooth, right, pleasant, and prosperous. The Amplified Bible says, "And He will make your paths straight and smooth [removing obstacles that block your way]." I like the way that the Passion translation puts these two verses.Proverbsâ¬ â3â¬:â5â¬-â6â¬ âTPTâ¬â¬"Trust in the Lord completely, and do not rely on your own opinions. With all your heart rely on him to guide you, and he will lead you in every decision you make. Become intimate with him in whatever you do, and he will lead you wherever you go."

Meditations on Proverbs 3 - Part 2Proverbs 3:3-4Let not steadfast love and faithfulness forsake you;bind them around your neck;write them on the tablet of your heart.So you will find favor and good successin the sight of God and man.Summary: If you want favor and success, be loving and faithful.Love and faithfulness go hand in hand. It is easy to say that you love someone, but faithfulness is the test that shows if that love is real. To find someone that is truly loving and faithful is to find a treasure.Proverbs 20:6Many a man proclaims his own steadfast love,but a faithful man who can find?Paul describes love as patient, bearing and enduring all things - meaning love does not give up when things get tough. It is faithful.1 Corinthians 13:4-7Love is patient and kind; love does not envy or boast; it is not arrogant or rude. It does not insist on its own way; it is not irritable or resentful; it does not rejoice at wrongdoing, but rejoices with the truth. Love bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.God shows this kind of love and faithfulness toward us.Lamentations 3:22-23The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases;his mercies never come to an end;they are new every morning;great is your faithfulness.As we draw closer to God and become more and more like Him, we can show this kind of love and faithfulness to others.Proverbs 3:3 shows a picture of love and faithfulness becoming more and more a part of us.- Don't let them forsake you. This implies putting forth effort to keep love and faithfulness close.- Bind them around your neck. Like a necklace is worn on the body and is visible for everyone to see, put on love and faithfulness and let people see the outward signs of these inner qualities.- Write them on the tablet of your heart. Make love and faithfulness become a part of who you are in your most inner being, as if they were written on your heart. As we grow in love and faithfulness, what will the result be?Proverbs 3:4So you will find favor and good success [lit. good understanding]in the sight of God and man.To have favor is to have the protection, provision, and influence that the one who favors you can provide.Genesis 6:8But Noah found favor in the eyes of the LORD. [and was delivered from the flood]Exodus 3:21And I will give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians; and when you go, you shall not go empty, [because the Egyptians will give the Israelites what they ask for]Ruth 2:13Then she [Ruth] said, "I have found favor in your eyes, my lord [Boaz], for you have comforted me and spoken kindly to your servant, though I am not one of your servants." [and Boaz married Ruth and provided for her]Esther 5:2And when the king saw Queen Esther standing in the court [even though it was against the law], she won favor in his sight, and he held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand. Then Esther approached and touched the tip of the scepter. [and the king allowed Esther to use his authority to save the Jews from annihilation.]To have favor and good understanding, means that the favor will continue. It's not a one-time thing based on a special situation, but a lasting favor based on a mutual understanding of your love and faithfulness. This favor and understanding ensures success with both God and man.

Meditations on Proverbs 3 - Part 1Proverbs 3:1-2 (ESV)My son, do not forget my teaching,but let your heart keep my commandments,for length of days and years of lifeand peace they will add to you.Summary: If you want a long peaceful life, keep God's commandments.In order to keep God's commandments, we must first know His teaching. And knowing it, we must continue to immerse ourselves in it so that we do not forget it. However, It's not enough to know God's commands, we must obey them and obey them from our heart.Deuteronomy 30:16 (ESV)If you obey the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you today, by loving the LORD your God, by walking in his ways, and by keeping his commandments and his statutes and his rules, then you shall live and multiply, and the LORD your God will bless you in the land that you are entering to take possession of it. Loving God and keeping His commands is tied to life and blessing. Conversely, if we do not keep His commands, we cannot expect to be blessed.Matthew 7:24-27 (ESV)"Everyone then who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house on the rock. And the rain fell, and the floods came, and the winds blew and beat on that house, but it did not fall, because it had been founded on the rock. And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them will be like a foolish man who built his house on the sand. And the rain fell, and the floods came, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell, and great was the fall of it."The man who built his house on the rock did so purposely (Luke says he dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock). The man who built on sand did not do so purposely, he just picked the most convenient and easy place and built a house without any foundation.God's teachings and commandments allow us to lay a careful foundation for our lives so that we can be secure even when the storms come. But we cannot haphazardly follow His commands as we feel like it. Our entire life must be based on letting His commands dictate our thoughts, words, and actions in all times, places, and circumstances.James 1:22-25 (AMP)But prove yourselves doers of the word [actively and continually obeying God's precepts], and not merely listeners [who hear the word but fail to internalize its meaning], deluding yourselves [by unsound reasoning contrary to the truth]. For if anyone only listens to the word without obeying it, he is like a man who looks very carefully at his natural face in a mirror; for once he has looked at himself and gone away, he immediately forgets what he looked like. But he who looks carefully into the perfect law, the law of liberty, and faithfully abides by it, not having become a [careless] listener who forgets but an active doer [who obeys], he will be blessed and favored by God in what he does [in his life of obedience].

content: Employers across the country (especially health care systems) are requiring Covid vaccines as a condition for employment. Just this week, my employer issued a notice that all employees will be required to get the Covid vaccine unless they have a religious or medical exemption. To be vaccinated or not should be a personal choice that individuals have the freedom to make. This decision should not be delegated to employers that believe that they know better than their employees or that a vaccinated workforce is more important than personal freedom. I work in Healthcare IT and I am concerned that many healthcare workers that choose not to get the vaccine will have difficulty finding work unless action is taken to prohibit discrimination based on vaccination status. For those that live in Wisconsin, there is a bill currently in the assembly that would prevent this type of discrimination. See https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/2021/proposals/reg/asm/bill/ab309. With every vaccine or medication, there is always risk. While the risk may be low, it is present. Where there is risk there must be choice.

content: H.R. 1, "The Politician Enrichment and Election Insecurity Act" - as Rep. Tom Tiffany calls it, recently passed the house and will likely be voted on the in the Senate soon. It's actually called the "For the People Act", but it seems to be more for politicians that don't want to be voted out of office. Contact your senators if you don't agree with this legislation.

The Equality Act, which recently passed in the US House of Representatives and will be voted on in the Senate is a threat to personal and religious liberty. In summary, the Equality Act does not allow any type of discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity. In practice, here are a few examples of what this means- A salon and spa that provides waxing services to women only, would have to provide services to a biological male that identifies as a woman.- A church men's group would have to allow biological females that identify as males to attend.- Transgender males would dominate woman's sports, because sports would be based on gender identity not biological gender- Biological men would be allowed into any female restroom or locker room if they identify as female (and vice versa).- A photographer could not decline to provide services at a same-sex wedding due to religious beliefs- A baker could not decline to make a gender transition celebration cake due to religious beliefsThe senate version of this bill is co-sponsored by Wisconsin's own Senator Tammy Baldwin. If you don't agree with this bill, contact your senators and ask them to vote no.

For those that live in Wisconsin, February is the primary election for the State Superintendent of Public Instruction. You can find out more about each of the candidates here https://docs.google.com/viewerng/viewer?url=https://wifamilyaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/State-Supt-Public-Instruction-Candidates-Primary-021621.pdf.Elections have consequences! content: I've been meditating on the first couple of verses of the book of John recently. "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God. All things were made through him and without him was not any thing made that was made." (John 1:1-3)I've been thinking specifically about the word "Word" and looked it up in one of my Bible study aids. This word is translated from the Greek word Logos. And while Logos does mean word, it also has a deeper meaning than that. It speaks to an inward collecting of thoughts and then speaking them, not in a single word, but in a speech, declaration, or command.This passage is talking about Jesus (as John 1:14 says, "the Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us..."), but it is also talking about the beginning. So it's interesting to compare John 1:1-3 with Genesis 1:1-26, where "God said" appears 8 separate times. John appears to be saying here that in the beginning God used his infinite creativity to imagine the perfect world and then speak it into existence through His Word - the Living Word - Jesus Christ.I think that what you believe about "In the beginning was the Word...and all things were made through him" affects your overall view of God. Is He a God who intricately designed all things and created them through His Word? And after the sin of man caused a curse to come upon this world, sent the same Word to become flesh (John 1:14) and redeem us from the curse (Galatians 3:13) so that we can have the hope of a perfect world once again (Revelation 21:4)?Or if, as some believe, the first chapters of Genesis are not to be taken literally, did God simply speak into existence the ability for chance to create, through ages of death and suffering, life that has only the appearance of design? Did the "Word become flesh" come to save us from death that came about because of Man's sin? Or was death an integral part of world from the beginning, a tool in the hand of chance to ensure that only the fittest survive?John seemed to believe the former (literal Genesis) and Paul echos a similar belief when he says "For since the creation of the world God's invisible qualities--his eternal power and divine nature--have been clearly seen, being understood from what has been made, so that people are without excuse." If the latter (metaphorical Genesis) were true, I think that it would result in a diminished view God and an erosion of the theology on which much of the New Testament rests.

Do you want to do great things in life? What seems like a great deed to us at the moment, may not be the same as what will actually be great in eternity. I was praying the other day asking God to show me His will for our family and feeling insignificant compared to the great heroes of the faith. What I felt that He said to me was, "Do the very best that you can in place that I have you right now." Being the very best employee or father or mother or wife or husband that you can be may seem ordinary. But if you are walking in obedience to God and doing your best, it is a great thing. Luke 16:10 says, "One who is faithful in a very little is also faithful in much, and one who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much." (ESV) What you are doing now may be paving the way for much greater things.Do you see a man (or woman) skillful and experienced in his work? He will stand [in honor] before kings; He will not stand before obscure men. Proverbs 22:29 (AMP)
